run.method: Savitzky-Golay detrend + astropy Box Least Squares

honesty: Nothing here is a planet discovery. Every signal is a candidate signal that needs professional follow-up.

validation.data: NASA TESS 2-minute cadence PDCSAP light curves

TOI 1338.readout: Matches the host stars' 14.6 d eclipsing-binary period, NOT the planet (TOI 1338 b is about 95 d). Correctly found the strongest signal; it is stellar. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up.

TOI 270.readout: Matches published TOI 270 c (5.66 d). Clean recovery of a known planet signal. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up.

TOI 216.readout: Unexplained. Known planets are at 17.16 d and 34.56 d. Possible aliasing between the two, or a false positive. V-shaped dip suggests binary contamination. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up. NOT a discovery.

TOI 175.readout: Correction (2026-10-18): this star was listed as TOI 776 by mistake. Its TIC ID, 307210830, is TOI 175 (L 98-59). The signal (3.6912 d) is close to the published period of L 98-59 c (3.6907 d, NASA Exoplanet Archive), but this result has not been re-reviewed by a human yet. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up. NOT a discovery.

TOI 700.readout: TOI 700 c again, consistent with the validation run. Clean recovery of a known planet signal. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up.

TOI 125.readout: Matches published TOI 125 b (4.65 d). Clean recovery of a known planet signal. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up.

TOI 193.readout: Correction (2026-10-18): this star was listed as TOI 849 by mistake. Its TIC ID, 183985250, is TOI 193 (LTT 9779). The signal (0.7926 d) is close to the published period of LTT 9779 b (0.79205 d, NASA Exoplanet Archive), but this result has not been re-reviewed by a human yet. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up. NOT a discovery.

TOI 178.readout: Weak (SNR 1.5), likely noise. No known planet at this period. Candidate signal, needs professional follow-up.
